Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning is a fully voiced action RPG with an open world and vibrant Fable/WoW-style visuals that aim for character over realism. Combat, magic and animations are top-notch, completely decimating Skyrim, but the soundtrack, story, dungeons, atmosphere and even quests are inferior.

Size and scope of the game are on an MMO scale with fast travel, a wonderful map system and a seemingly endless supply of side quests. There's no feeling of grinding but much of the content does feel like filler and, if you stray from the storyline too long, the repetitiveness and single-player MMO feeling will hit.

With loot that feels like Diablo-lite, with randomized stats, set pieces and uniques to be found; skills such as lockpicking, persuasion, stealth and detect hidden, all with perks at certain points; warrior, rogue and mage ability trees a la WoW talents; and crafting systems of alchemy, gems/sockets and blacksmithing, Kingdoms of Amalur is an RPG through and through.

Overall, a wonderful game if you like being set free to do your own thing but can accept the pitfalls that tend to come with open-world RPGs.

Before its release to Steam, I played hours upon hours of Kingdoms of Amalur for the Xbox 360, and I can tell you my experiences with this game had me loving it more and more each time I played it. KoA is a fresh take on the RPG Adventure games we're so used to playing, this one in particular giving us a very unique character that develops based upon your choices and decisions. Instead of listing the pro's and con's of this game in a bullet layered format, I'll instead give an in-depth analysis of what this game has to offer for you potential buyers!

Main Story:
Right off the bat, the main story line leaves you in suspense as you traverse further to figure out 'Who you really are', and 'What really happened.' I will refrain from giving out spoilers, but the entirety of the main quest line has an interesting plot, in which the character has many ways of going about, all leading up until that moment where you fulfill your goals and get your questions answered! The questline is not generic in any way, other than the fact that you find yourself broken, defeated, and lost in a world in which you have to learn, once again, about where you came from, and what it is you're meant to do. All of this becomes apparent as you meet new key characters along the way that help guide you on your path without giving you too much to lean on in the beginning of the game. That being said, delving into the questline in order to find the truth was truly captivating to me, and I enjoyed each and every quest from start to finish. 

Side Quests:
While the side quests are always completely optional, I can't stress it enough that actually taking the time to do them is both fun and rewarding! Several factions are mapped out across The Faelands that have their own unique and interesting questlines, not to mention the incredible rewards each has to give! These Factions are not the only side quests given within the game, as there are other civilian and non-dynamic character quests that are given throughout the entire game. Some quests can be tedious, but unlike other games, these tedious quests truly do reap great rewards for the character. Not only will completing a quest leave you with a bit more gold in your pocket, or an extra item to equip, but completing these side quests will increase your relationship with other npc's, sometimes so much so that they will be willing to share a few items of their own with you. All in all, the side quests are incredibly refreshing, and add a bit more flavor to the game when you're not so interested in just following the main story line. 

Dungeons:
This is something that I can't really express much love or hate for, as the dungeons in Kingdoms of Amalur were honestly satisfactory, for me at least. Each dungeon, while very different, had extremely generic layouts and areas that had no unique flavor setting them apart, other than perhaps the loot acquired from each of them. Don't get me wrong, the layout is beautiful and it does give you that dungeonesque feeling, but when it comes down to it, I just don't feel like they added enough diversity. Other than the aesthetics, the rewards given in each dungeon speak of their own value, as you'll never be left empty-handed for completing one. 

Combat system: 
I've finally reached my favorite aspect of the game... the combat. I absolutely love the combat to this game, possibly due to the fact that, well, its insanely unique! There are no set combos or time frames that it takes for your character to swing or attack. YOU attack when YOU want to attack, and this aspect of combat really gives you a sense of control and realism with your character. The different weapons and unique patterns of attacks offered for each type of weapon is absolutely awestriking. My first time using the chakrams and seeing how flashy and insane the moveset was really set that weapon apart from the rest. Not only do you have the ability to create your own combinations, you can tie your combination in with two different weapons, making the number of combinations unexhaustable. A staff and a sword, or a chakram and a great hammer, a wand, a greatsword, faeblades, a bow, so on and so forth! This all ties in well with the fact that you are not limited by your imagination to throw magic, or any spells in the mix. This truly gives your character a sense of value, as you are, within reason, your own, indistinguishable person. 

Gear/Crafting:
I really enjoyed some of the gear sets in the game, and you always have that excited feeling when you pick up a piece that has better stats, and just looks plain awesome! Starting out, your gear will obviously be mediocre, but that doesn't take away the fact that these sets 'get the job done.' Each new piece of gear is unique in its own way, and when we add gem sockets and enchants to the mix, you will find an entirely different craft all together. The crafting system works in a systematic way where you'll need to acquire several pieces of equipment that have 'matching qualities' before you can create your new weapon or armor piece. Of course, this goes without saying, the better equipment you have and the higher your skill, the better your gear will be when you make that fresh new piece. Adding gems to gear in order to give your character some type of buff, whether it be increased mana, or extra burn damage, etc, is always satisfying, and lets not forget to mention... You can name a piece after you craft it. I don't know about you, but I love giving names to gear of my craft to give it that unique and one of a kind feeling. All in all, the gear in the game is not sorely lacking, but I will say that there was room for improvement on the aestheitc aspect of it, such as maybe adding more flair to a crafted piece or unique piece, but that aside, the gear in the game, as well as the crafting system, is rather balanced.

Skill Tree/Perks:
Could I go ON about how I love the skill tree in this game... While there are not an infinite number of talents, there sure seems to be an infinite number of ways you can build your character. With the three main skill trees, (Might, Finesse, and Sorcery) you can literally build your character any way you want. There are multiple different fate cards for each type of build, so there is never a scenario where you'll feel unrewarded for going into this tree, that tree, and the other. You will always be compensated for the way you spec, so much so that you'll recieve your own unique buff while you traverse farther down your own unique spec. The perks, too, have very rewarding qualities to them, giving you a plethora of options for how you want to build your character so they fit to your liking. Whether it be increased chance to lock pick, or finding hidden treasures with ease, all of these different perks really are rewarding in their own way. 

There are many other aspects of this game that can be talked about, but I believe that the true value of this games comes within the eye of the beholder, so I'll stop this review here. If you're looking for a fun, refreshing game, Kingdoms of Amalur brings the package to the table. The cartoonish graphics and unique gameplay give this game its own unique flair, and the story only becomes more exciting with the DLC content as you explore different and unique areas to the game with their own interesting storylines and rewards! I hope this basic review helps you decide whether or not you want to take a peek at KoA: Reckoning. With that being said, I wish you luck, fateless ones!

Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning is basically a third-person "solo MMO" (yes, this sounds strange, but you'll understand soon enough).

It takes many elements from MMORPGs — huge fantasy zones, quest hubs, tons of loot, character progression, and a constant sense of adventure — but turns them into a single-player RPG experience. The result is a surprisingly accessible and addictive fantasy adventure.

The world of Amalur is colorful, rich in lore, and filled with countless quests to discover. The combat is probably the game's greatest strength, with fast and satisfying action, a great variety of weapons, and a flexible class system that allows you to create different builds.

Of course, it has some flaws. The story and some quests can feel less memorable compared to other great RPGs, and the open world is more a collection of large areas than a completely free sandbox.

Despite that, Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning remains a very enjoyable fantasy RPG with a unique identity. If you are looking for a colorful adventure with satisfying combat, lots of exploration, and that classic MMO feeling in a solo experience, give it a try.
